note:
What each sentence is ABOUT. Assigned by hand from the sentence alone, before looking at any reader's score, using the same seven categories on both documents. This is an author taxonomy and it is a judgment: clause 6 of the hero note ('the third consecutive year such costs have been described as non-recurring') could reasonably be filed under performance rather than language, and clause 15 of the held-out note (a convertible's conversion price) under shareholder rather than debt. The test of whether the taxonomy is doing real work is that reader profiles built on it hold across two unrelated documents — an arbitrary labelling would not survive that.

THE REAL FILING STRAINS THE TAXONOMY IN THREE PLACES, recorded here rather than fixed by inventing an eighth category. (1) Three clauses of whirlpool-q2 are segment headers — 'MDA NORTH AMERICA' and its two siblings — which are structural labels rather than statements about the business, and fit none of the seven. They are filed under the topic of the block they head, which is performance. They are kept as clauses at all because without them three segment bullets read as unattributed percentages. (2) Clause 28 is a tax rate, and tax has no category; filed under performance as the nearest, since it is what turns EBIT into earnings. (3) Clause 23, 'EPS is revised to reflect the new interest expense', is filed under debt rather than share because the cause is the cost of borrowing, and clause 16's Brazil tax-case gain under language rather than performance because it is a one-off supporting a margin. Both are arguable in the same way the two calls named above are.

THE DISTRIBUTION IS THE MORE INTERESTING RESULT. On whirlpool-q2 the seven categories split 13 performance, 8 language, 4 debt, 3 events, and exactly one clause each of cash, per share and who it depends on. The two constructed notes spread far more evenly across the same seven — meridian-q4 runs 7 performance, 6 debt, 6 events, 4 language, 3 cash, 2 per share, 2 dependency, and aldercroft-h1 leads on dependency with 5, then 4 performance and 3 debt, with 2 in each of the rest. A genuine earnings release is overwhelmingly performance narration and management framing; the balance the constructed notes have is a property of documents written by someone who knew what the readers were for. Two consequences: the taxonomy covers a real filing without being widened, and topic lift on cash, per share and dependency rests on a single clause each there, so those three bars should not be read as profile evidence on this document.

categories.debt: What is owed — leverage, covenants, maturities, facilities, drawn and undrawn
categories.cash: Cash generation and working capital — conversion, receivables, deferred revenue
categories.perform: How the business did — revenue, margin, earnings, growth, guidance
categories.share: What accrues to a share — buybacks, dividends, dilution, compensation
categories.depend: Who the revenue depends on — concentration, renewal, retention, churn
categories.language: How management characterises things — hedges, denials, adjustments called non-recurring
categories.events: Things that happened — people, incidents, acquisitions, projects
